observation.initial_state: At t=0 the clip is already mid-process: a yellow-green tennis ball sits low inside a dense cloud of red particulate powder that forms a tight, well-defined elliptical veil around the string bed of a racket. The racket is tilted with its throat/handle toward the lower-left; the background is an out-of-focus green field and a dark upper region. The ball's seam is visible, indicating it is not perfectly still.
visible_changes: Early (frames 1-5): the ball is centered within the powder veil, which still hugs the strings with a crisp rim; the ball begins to climb slightly and the seam orientation shifts, showing rotation.

Middle (frames 6-13): the ball rises steadily above the powder ring, moving toward the top of the frame; the powder cloud loses its sharp elliptical edge and starts to billow and spread, becoming more diffuse; the racket and background horizon drift toward the lower-left of the frame, indicating the camera is tilting/panning upward to follow the ball.

Late (frames 14-21): the ball reaches the top edge and is partly cut off, clearly separated from and above the powder; the red cloud has expanded into a soft, wide, dissipating plume with no coherent rim; the strung racket has largely moved out of the lower view, leaving mostly the upper powder arc and the handle at the lower-left. The ball's seam keeps reorienting throughout, consistent with ongoing spin.
observation.final_state: The ball is at the very top of the frame, partially out of view, hovering above a now widely dispersed, faint red powder cloud; the racket's string bed is mostly off-screen and the powder no longer retains its original tight ring shape.
uncertain_details: Whether the ball's upward motion is its own launch or partly camera tracking cannot be fully separated, though the ball-racket gap grows, so the ball is moving away from the racket.
The cause of the powder cloud and whether any contact preceded frame 1 are not shown; the process is already ongoing at t=0.
The material identity of the red powder and of the ball surface is not determinable from the images.
It is not certain whether the racket itself is stationary or also moving, since camera motion and object motion both shift the racket within the frame.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
The images are chronological samples of the exact training clip, not its full source video.
Describe visible initial state, changes over the sequence, final state, and important unchanged
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame. Static intervals are valid. Do not supply named physics laws.
Return JSON {"initial_state":"...", "visible_changes":["chronological observation with early/middle/late evidence"],
"final_state":"...", "uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English.
